current_row.boundary_rationale: A third named figure opens the unit, וְאֶל שְׁמַעְיָ֥הוּ הַנֶּחֱלָמִ֖י תֹּאמַ֥ר לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.29.24, byte), matching “Concerning Shemaiah the Nehelamite you shall speak, saying,” (web:Jer.29.24) — the unit’s own front seam opens on the conjunctive וְאֶל, a byte-true continuity signal disclosed here rather than passed over; it does not argue against the cut because it is the ordinary narrative connective introducing Jeremiah’s next commissioned reply rather than a continuation of the address just closed — the addressee shifts at once to Shemaiah the Nehelamite, commissioned as the subject of Jeremiah’s own reply rather than addressed directly, the tier-1 signal the seam actually rests on. Yahweh’s own governing formula opens this stretch of the reply, כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Jer.29.25, byte), a koh-amar-headed member of the full title-stack object (sweep: 31 verses book-wide, skeleton tier), governing the charge that אַתָּה֩ שָׁלַ֨חְתָּ בְשִׁמְכָ֜ה סְפָרִ֗ים (oshb:Jer.29.25, byte) — letters, plural, the medium the bytes actually carry here, distinct from the single letter Zephaniah reads back at the report’s own close. The reply quotes Shemaiah’s own hostile letter back at him, including its rebuke naming Jeremiah by his home village, וְעַתָּ֗ה לָ֚מָּה לֹ֣א גָעַ֔רְתָּ בְּיִרְמְיָ֖הוּ הָֽעֲנְּתֹתִ֑י הַמִּתְנַבֵּ֖א לָכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.29.27, byte), matching “Now therefore, why have you not rebuked Jeremiah of Anathoth, who makes himself a prophet to you,” (web:Jer.29.27) — a defective spelling of the gentilic naming that village. It closes on a narrative report explaining how this exchange became known, וַיִּקְרָ֛א צְפַנְיָ֥ה הַכֹּהֵ֖ן אֶת הַסֵּ֣פֶר הַזֶּ֑ה בְּאָזְנֵ֖י יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִֽיא (oshb:Jer.29.29, byte), matching “Zephaniah the priest read this letter in the hearing of Jeremiah the prophet.” (web:Jer.29.29). A fresh word-event formula opens at verse 30, turning from this narrative report to Yahweh’s own word to Jeremiah, and the row does not extend past that opening.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Closing this row at verse 28, immediately after the quoted content of Shemaiah’s own letter, and reading verse 29 as the opening of the row that follows, was rejected because verse 29’s report refers back to this letter by name and completes the account of how it was heard, rather than introducing the fresh word-event formula that actually opens the next unit at verse 30.
current_row.literature_type_guess: Jeremiah’s reply quoting a rival letter against him
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
current_row.device_notes: A setumah marks the preceding span’s own close, immediately before this unit’s own opening, at oshb:Jer.29.23 (a single-witness WLC mark; corroboration alone, weak under the Prophets addendum); a petuchah closes this unit itself at oshb:Jer.29.29. The gentilic naming Jeremiah’s home village at verse 27 is written in the defective spelling the bytes actually carry, disclosed here rather than silently normalized to a fuller form.

As written the digit is attached to the full title-stack object, whose swept count is 32.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh koh-amar opens the unit, כִּי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה ק֥וֹל חֲרָדָ֖ה שָׁמָ֑עְנוּ פַּ֖חַד וְאֵ֥ין שָׁלֽוֹם (oshb:Jer.30.5, byte), matching “For Yahweh says:” (web:Jer.30.5) “We have heard a voice of trembling; a voice of fear, and not of peace.” (web:Jer.30.5) — a communal cry of dread rather than a report about a third party. The day named next carries the hoy interjection in its own DAY-ALAS shape, not a woe-oracle onset: ה֗וֹי כִּ֥י גָד֛וֹל הַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא מֵאַ֣יִן כָּמֹ֑הוּ וְעֵֽת צָרָ֥ה הִיא֙ לְיַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וּמִמֶּ֖נָּה יִוָּשֵֽׁעַ (oshb:Jer.30.7, byte), matching “Alas, for that day is great, so that none is like it! It is even the time of Jacob’s trouble; but he will be saved out of it.” (web:Jer.30.7) — an exclamation over the day's own severity rather than a pronounced judgment against a named party, closing already on the promise of rescue rather than on threat alone. Jacob's name in this same verse carries the defective spelling these bytes attest. A day-formula turn follows at verse 8, וְהָיָה֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא נְאֻ֣ם יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת אֶשְׁבֹּ֤ר עֻלּוֹ֙ מֵעַ֣ל צַוָּארֶ֔ךָ וּמוֹסְרוֹתֶ֖יךָ אֲנַתֵּ֑ק וְלֹא יַעַבְדוּ ב֥וֹ ע֖וֹד זָרִֽים (oshb:Jer.30.8, byte), matching “It will come to pass in that day, says Yahweh of Armies, that I will break his yoke from off your neck, and will burst your bonds. Strangers will no more make them their bondservants;” (web:Jer.30.8) — the second-person singular marking here is real but mixed with a third-person suffix in the same clause and a third-person reference closing the same verse; a full neum-YHWH-tsevaot stack sits inside this same verse, corroborating rather than opening a fresh unit, since no koh-amar or date-formula onset of its own accompanies it. The rescue promise continues through the same defective spelling of Jacob's name twice over, וְאַתָּ֡ה אַל תִּירָא֩ עַבְדִּ֨י יַעֲקֹ֤ב נְאֻם יְהֹוָה֙ וְאַל תֵּחַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֠י הִנְנִ֤י מוֹשִֽׁיעֲךָ֙ מֵֽרָח֔וֹק וְאֶֽת זַרְעֲךָ֖ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ שִׁבְיָ֑ם וְשָׁ֧ב יַעֲקֹ֛ב וְשָׁקַ֥ט וְשַׁאֲנַ֖ן וְאֵ֥ין מַחֲרִֽיד (oshb:Jer.30.10, byte), matching “Therefore don’t be afraid, O Jacob my servant, says Yahweh. Don’t be dismayed, Israel. For, behold, I will save you from afar, and save your offspring from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return, and will be quiet and at ease. No one will make him afraid.” (web:Jer.30.10). It closes on כִּֽי אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י נְאֻם יְהוָ֖ה לְהֽוֹשִׁיעֶ֑ךָ כִּי֩ אֶעֱשֶׂ֨ה כָלָ֜ה בְּכָֽל הַגּוֹיִ֣ם אֲשֶׁ֧ר הֲפִצוֹתִ֣יךָ שָּׁ֗ם אַ֤ךְ אֹֽתְךָ֙ לֹֽא אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה כָלָ֔ה וְיִסַּרְתִּ֨יךָ֙ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֔ט וְנַקֵּ֖ה לֹ֥א אֲנַקֶּֽךָּ (oshb:Jer.30.11, byte), matching “For I am with you, says Yahweh, to save you; for I will make a full end of all the nations where I have scattered you, but I will not make a full end of you; but I will correct you in measure, and will in no way leave you unpunished.” (web:Jer.30.11). A second fresh koh-amar turns the address to a feminine-singular figure at verse 12, and this row stops there.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting a fresh row at verse 8's own bayom-hahu turn to the broken yoke was considered: that verse carries the span's first second-person singular marking, אֶשְׁבֹּ֤ר עֻלּוֹ֙ מֵעַ֣ל צַוָּארֶ֔ךָ וּמוֹסְרוֹתֶ֖יךָ אֲנַתֵּ֑ק (oshb:Jer.30.8, byte); it is rejected because no koh-amar or date-formula onset stands at that verse, the marking is mixed with a third-person suffix in the same clause and a third-person reference closing the same verse, the person layer reverts to third person at the very next verse, וְעָ֣בְד֔וּ אֵ֖ת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶ֑ם וְאֵת֙ דָּוִ֣ד (oshb:Jer.30.9, byte), and the first vocative addressee in the unit stands only two verses later, וְאַתָּ֡ה אַל תִּירָא֩ עַבְדִּ֨י יַעֲקֹ֤ב (oshb:Jer.30.10, byte); the day-formula opening the verse is a day-alas-adjacent shape distinct from the year-header date object and stands in 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys), so it is not read here as a date-formula onset. The day-formula turn is left as one of this stretch's unresolved internal questions rather than folded into either reading.
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
current_row.device_notes: The inventory carries nothing at the seam where this span opens, oshb:Jer.30.4. A setumah falls inside the span at oshb:Jer.30.9 (WLC, single-witness; modest tier-3 support under the Prophets addendum), and a petuchah closes the span itself at oshb:Jer.30.11 (same tier and witness). A paseq also falls at oshb:Jer.30.8 and a second at oshb:Jer.30.11 (sourced from WLC alone; a single-witness seg-layer occurrence count, silent on the paseq’s placement inside the verse). The hoy at verse 7 is disclosed here by its own day-alas role, distinct from the book's woe-oracle onsets elsewhere and from its funeral-cry and sword-apostrophe shapes. A second-person plural imperative pair opens the interior comparison, שַׁאֲלוּ נָ֣א (oshb:Jer.30.6, byte), standing inside the span without a fresh koh-amar of its own.

findings.defective_text: P11-002: 'A second-person plural imperative pair opens the interior comparison, שַׁאֲלוּ נָ֣א (oshb:Jer.30.6, byte)'; P12-007: the rationale splice at oshb:Jer.33.10 stops at אַתֶּ֣ם while its gloss reads 'about which you say'
findings.byte_evidence: Gloss extent exceeds splice extent at both sites. Jer.30.6 opens שַׁאֲלוּ נָ֣א וּרְא֔וּ (byte tier): the imperative pair is the first and third words, and the splice covers only the first imperative plus the entreaty particle. At Jer.33.10 the construction the gloss renders is three words -- the same row's device_notes quotes it in full and sweeps it (2 verses byte tier, 3 verses skeleton tier: Jer.32.36, Jer.32.43, Jer.33.10) -- but the rationale splice drops the third word.
findings.proposed_cure: Re-cut each splice to the extent its gloss claims: carry the second imperative into the Jer.30.6 splice and the third word into the Jer.33.10 splice.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh koh-amar opens a jubilant summons, כִּי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה רָנּ֤וּ לְיַֽעֲקֹב֙ שִׂמְחָ֔ה וְצַהֲל֖וּ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ הַגּוֹיִ֑ם הַשְׁמִ֤יעוּ הַֽלְלוּ֙ וְאִמְר֔וּ הוֹשַׁ֤ע יְהוָה֙ אֶֽת עַמְּךָ֔ אֵ֖ת שְׁאֵרִ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Jer.31.7, byte), matching “For Yahweh says,” (web:Jer.31.7) “Sing with gladness for Jacob, and shout for the chief of the nations. Publish, praise, and say, ‘Yahweh, save your people, the remnant of Israel!’” (web:Jer.31.7) — a call to sing rather than a scene description; this same verse also carries a paseq. The messenger formula stands behind a subordinating particle, כִּי (oshb:Jer.31.7, byte) — the same particle that opens the verse immediately before this span, כִּ֣י יֶשׁ י֔וֹם (oshb:Jer.31.6, byte), and the ground-clause inside the span, כִּֽי פָדָ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.31.11, byte); disclosed here as continuity across the front seam, the particle-prefixed formula shape is unremarkable in itself (sweep: 29 verses, consonantal tier, MT keys) and drives nothing on its own. The regathering closes its first movement on kinship language, בִּבְכִ֣י יָבֹ֗אוּ וּֽבְתַחֲנוּנִים֮ אֽוֹבִילֵם֒ אֽוֹלִיכֵם֙ אֶל נַ֣חֲלֵי מַ֔יִם בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ יָשָׁ֔ר לֹ֥א יִכָּשְׁל֖וּ בָּ֑הּ כִּֽי הָיִ֤יתִי לְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְאָ֔ב וְאֶפְרַ֖יִם בְּכֹ֥רִי הֽוּא (oshb:Jer.31.9, byte), matching “They will come with weeping. I will lead them with petitions. I will cause them to walk by rivers of waters, in a straight way in which they won’t stumble; for I am a father to Israel. Ephraim is my firstborn.” (web:Jer.31.9) — Ephraim named as firstborn. An imperative to the nations follows without any koh-amar of its own, שִׁמְע֤וּ דְבַר יְהוָה֙ גּוֹיִ֔ם וְהַגִּ֥ידוּ בָאִיִּ֖ים מִמֶּרְחָ֑ק וְאִמְר֗וּ מְזָרֵ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יְקַבְּצֶ֔נּוּ וּשְׁמָר֖וֹ כְּרֹעֶ֥ה עֶדְרֽוֹ (oshb:Jer.31.10, byte), matching “Hear Yahweh’s word, you nations, and declare it in the distant islands. Say, ‘He who scattered Israel will gather him, and keep him, as a shepherd does his flock.’” (web:Jer.31.10); it is bound forward by its own ‘for’-clause at verse 11 into the same regathering announcement rather than opening an independent unit. The oil-and-grain imagery names the new wine by its own distinct term, tirosh rather than yayin, וּבָאוּ֮ וְרִנְּנ֣וּ בִמְרוֹם צִיּוֹן֒ וְנָהֲר֞וּ אֶל ט֣וּב יְהוָ֗ה עַל דָּגָן֙ וְעַל תִּירֹ֣שׁ וְעַל יִצְהָ֔ר וְעַל בְּנֵי צֹ֖אן וּבָקָ֑ר וְהָיְתָ֤ה נַפְשָׁם֙ כְּגַ֣ן רָוֶ֔ה וְלֹא יוֹסִ֥יפוּ לְדַאֲבָ֖ה עֽוֹד (oshb:Jer.31.12, byte), matching “They will come and sing in the height of Zion, and will flow to the goodness of Yahweh, to the grain, to the new wine, to the oil, and to the young of the flock and of the herd. Their soul will be as a watered garden. They will not sorrow any more at all.” (web:Jer.31.12). It closes on וְרִוֵּיתִ֛י נֶ֥פֶשׁ הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים דָּ֑שֶׁן וְעַמִּ֛י אֶת טוּבִ֥י יִשְׂבָּ֖עוּ נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.31.14, byte), matching “I will satiate the soul of the priests with fatness, and my people will be satisfied with my goodness,” says Yahweh. (web:Jer.31.14). A fresh koh-amar turns to Rachel's own weeping at verse 15, and this row ends just ahead of that turn.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting a fresh row at verse 10's own imperative to the nations was weighed, since שִׁמְע֤וּ דְבַר יְהוָה֙ גּוֹיִ֔ם וְהַגִּ֥ידוּ (oshb:Jer.31.10, byte) does open with an explicit vocative addressee; it is rejected because the summons functions as a call to relay a message rather than a change of the unit's own subject, the content it introduces reverting at once to third-person description of Israel's own regathering, מְזָרֵ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יְקַבְּצֶ֔נּוּ (oshb:Jer.31.10, byte), matching the third-person material standing on both sides of it, with the tier-3 setumah recorded at oshb:Jer.31.9, single-witness and weak, standing at this same declined seam as corroboration rather than as a driver; this alternative is held only at reduced confidence rather than adopted.
current_row.literature_type_guess: jubilant regathering summons for the remnant
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
current_row.device_notes: A petuchah sits at the seam where this span opens, oshb:Jer.31.6, recurs inside the span at oshb:Jer.31.9 as a setumah, and a further setumah closes the span itself at oshb:Jer.31.14 (WLC, single-witness throughout; under the Prophets-addendum rule, this stands as tier-3 corroboration, and weak). current_row.boundary_rationale: The unit opens with a divine first-person hearing-report that names the figure in the third person before any quoted speech begins, שָׁמ֣וֹעַ שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי אֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ מִתְנוֹדֵ֔ד (oshb:Jer.31.18, byte) — the quoted speech itself starting at the fifth word, יִסַּרְתַּ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Jer.31.18, byte) — matching “I have surely heard Ephraim grieving thus, ‘You have chastised me, and I was chastised, as an untrained calf. Turn me, and I will be turned, for you are Yahweh my God.” (web:Jer.31.18) — Ephraim's own self-address, reported as overheard rather than described from outside. The confession continues in his own voice, כִּֽי אַחֲרֵ֤י שׁוּבִי֙ נִחַ֔מְתִּי וְאַֽחֲרֵי֙ הִוָּ֣דְעִ֔י סָפַ֖קְתִּי עַל יָרֵ֑ךְ בֹּ֚שְׁתִּי וְגַם נִכְלַ֔מְתִּי כִּ֥י נָשָׂ֖אתִי חֶרְפַּ֥ת נְעוּרָֽי (oshb:Jer.31.19, byte), matching “Surely after that I was turned. I repented. After that I was instructed. I struck my thigh. I was ashamed, yes, even confounded, because I bore the reproach of my youth.’” (web:Jer.31.19) — shame and the reproach of youth, named directly. It closes on the father's own answer, הֲבֵן֩ יַקִּ֨יר לִ֜י אֶפְרַ֗יִם אִ֚ם יֶ֣לֶד שַׁעֲשֻׁעִ֔ים כִּֽי מִדֵּ֤י דַבְּרִי֙ בּ֔וֹ זָכֹ֥ר אֶזְכְּרֶ֖נּוּ ע֑וֹד עַל כֵּ֗ן הָמ֤וּ מֵעַי֙ ל֔וֹ רַחֵ֥ם אֲֽרַחֲמֶ֖נּוּ נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.31.20, byte), matching “Is Ephraim my dear son? Is he a darling child? For as often as I speak against him, I still earnestly remember him. Therefore my heart yearns for him. I will surely have mercy on him,” says Yahweh. (web:Jer.31.20).
